task.description:
WF-03 Step 3c -- SECURITY GATE on the ISS-0109 implementation (commits 5556767 / 8367b4d on
feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821). Review the DIFF, not the developer's account of it:
`git diff 70736d5..HEAD -- test/` plus `git diff 70736d5..HEAD --stat`.

WHAT SHIPPED: one new test-only module test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (Letflow.TenantFixture)
and its adoption in exactly two test modules (test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs,
test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs). The gate-approved design is
lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md.

FIRST, RUN YOUR OWN SCOPE TEST AND STATE THE VERDICT EXPLICITLY. ELIXIR-DEV and the design
both assert this change touches NO tenant-data path -- no lib/ change at all, test-only code.
If that holds, most of INV-1..INV-8 are NOT-APPLICABLE and saying so per invariant is the
correct output; do not manufacture findings to justify the step. But VERIFY the premise
yourself rather than inheriting it: confirm from the diff that lib/ is genuinely untouched
(the design artefact itself is the only permitted lib/ path), and that the new module is
never referenced from shipped code and never enters lib/letflow/application.ex's supervision
tree.

THEN CHECK THE TWO INVARIANTS THE DESIGN ITSELF WROTE, because they are the reason this gate
runs at all on a test-only change -- this helper issues raw SQL against a multi-tenant
database:

INV-F-8 (design SS4): every query the helper issues is either (a) parameterized and scoped to
the single tenant/schema under test, or (b) a read of Postgres catalog metadata
(information_schema.schemata / information_schema.tables) filtered by table_schema = $1. No
value belonging to another tenant is ever read, logged, or returned. NO UNSCOPED CATALOG
ENUMERATION. Check every query in the new module against this, one by one. An unscoped
catalog read in a test helper is not harmless: it would make the failure-capture report leak
other tenants' schema names into logs, and this repo already has ISS-0111/GH#365 open for a
test that mutates shared tenant state globally.

INV-F-9 (design SS4): the ONLY raw-SQL identifier interpolation is DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS
"<name>" CASCADE and "<name>".schema_migrations, and <name> is ALWAYS the output of
TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 -- never a caller-supplied string. Everything else
is $1-parameterized. Verify by reading every interpolation site in the new file. This is the
same argument tenant_provisioning.ex:180-187 already makes for production; confirm the helper
actually earns it rather than merely claiming it.

ALSO CHECK, since it is a new logging surface: the teardown log line the helper emits at :info
carries schema name, tenant_id, schema_present_before_drop, test module and test name. Confirm
it contains NOTHING beyond the tenant under test -- no other tenant's identifiers, no
credentials, no connection string, no arbitrary exception text. A capture/logging helper is
exactly where a leak would be introduced casually and would then be copied into 39 more call
sites later (ISS-0112).

CONSTRAINTS: you gate, you do not edit. Report per-invariant verdicts (APPLIES PASS / APPLIES
FAIL / NOT-APPLICABLE with the reason). Toolchain here is Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 against a
1.18.3-otp-27 pin (ISS-0106, filed, not yours) -- plain `mix compile` only, no
--warnings-as-errors, no `mix format`. Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821; commit by explicit filename.
acceptance_criteria: An explicit scope verdict is stated, derived from the diff rather than from ELIXIR-DEV's claim: whether this change touches a tenant-data path, including confirmation that lib/ is untouched apart from the design artefact and that Letflow.TenantFixture is never referenced from shipped code or added to the supervision tree
A per-invariant verdict (APPLIES PASS / APPLIES FAIL / NOT-APPLICABLE with reason) is given for INV-1 through INV-8

INV-F-8 is checked query by query against the new module: every query is either tenant/schema-scoped and parameterized, or a catalog read filtered by table_schema = $1, with no unscoped catalog enumeration

INV-F-9 is checked interpolation site by interpolation site: the only raw-SQL identifier interpolation is the schema name from TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1, never a caller-supplied string

The new teardown log line's contents are checked field by field and confirmed to carry nothing beyond the tenant under test -- no other tenant's identifiers, no credentials, no connection string, no arbitrary exception text
A single overall verdict (PASS or FAIL) is stated; on FAIL each finding names the specific line and the invariant it violates

result.summary: SECURITY GATE PASS. SCOPE VERDICT, derived from the diff and not from ELIXIR-DEV's claim: this change does NOT touch a shipped tenant-data path, but it is NOT out of scope either -- it introduces raw SQL against tenant schemas in test-only code, so INV-1, INV-6 and INV-7 were run for real rather than skipped. Evidence: git diff 70736d5..HEAD --name-only yields six paths; filtering for code under lib/, priv/ or config/ (grep -E '^(lib|priv|config)/.*[.]exs?$') returns NONE -- the only lib/ path is the design artefact lib/letflow/design/iss0109-...md, whose diff is 2 documentation hunks (+7/-6) correcting two invariant citations and containing no code. No migration under priv/repo/migrations/, no API route, no response-shaping code, no lookup-by-ID handler, no secret-resolving config. grep -rn 'TenantFixture' lib/ priv/ config/ (excluding /design/) returns NONE, and the only three files in the whole tree referencing Letflow.TenantFixture are the module itself plus the two adopting test modules -- so it is never referenced from shipped code. It is not in lib/letflow/application.ex's supervision tree (that file is not in the diff at all, and the module is a plain module -- no use GenServer, no child_spec, no start_link). mix.exs:20 compiles test/support only under elixirc_paths(:test), so the module does not exist in a non-test build. INV-F-8 (query-by-query, all five Repo.query! sites plus three Ecto sites in test/support/tenant_fixture.ex): EARNED. :545 SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.schemata WHERE schema_name = $1 -- catalog read, filtered, $1-bound. :555 SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = $1 AND table_type = 'BASE TABLE' -- catalog read, filtered by table_schema = $1 exactly as the invariant requires, $1-bound. :568 SELECT version FROM "<schema>".schema_migrations -- physically confined to the one tenant schema. :580 SELECT now() at time zone 'utc' and :585 SELECT pg_backend_pid() -- no tenant data of any kind. :469 Repo.get_by(Registration, tenant_id: tenant_id) and :337/:338 Repo.delete_all(from(r in Registration, where: r.tenant_id == ^tenant_id)) / Repo.delete_all(from(t in Tenant, where: t.id == ^tenant_id)) -- Ecto parameterized and scoped to the single tenant under test. THERE IS NO UNSCOPED CATALOG ENUMERATION: every information_schema read carries a WHERE on the tenant's own schema name, so no other tenant's schema or table names can enter the capture report. Contrast worth recording: this is precisely the defect ISS-0111/GH#365 has open against identity_migration_test's unfiltered bulk DELETE, and the new helper does not reproduce it -- both of its deletes are tenant-predicated. INV-F-9 (site-by-site): EARNED, and provably rather than by declaration. The file contains exactly TWO raw-SQL identifier interpolations: :331 DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS "<schema_name>" CASCADE and :568 SELECT version FROM "<schema_name>".schema_migrations. In BOTH, schema_name is bound immediately upstream from TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 -- at the enclosing case in teardown/2 (:326-332) and at :457 in do_capture/2 -- and never from any other source. That function (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:100-106) is Ecto.UUID.cast/1 followed by "tenant_" <> hex, so its success output is structurally confined to ^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$ and cannot carry a quote or any other injection character; its :error branch is handled, not interpolated. I traced the three caller-supplied opts that carry strings -- :slug_prefix and :display_name (:175-176) reach the DB only through Tenant.create_changeset/3 + Repo.insert! (parameterized), and :expected_tables (:177) is used only in the pure list subtraction at :498 and in inspect/1 output -- so no caller-supplied string reaches raw SQL on any path. Note the Registration.schema_name value returned by provision!/1 (:305) is DB-sourced but is only placed in the returned map, never interpolated. TEARDOWN LOG LINE (:356-360), field by field: @marker is a fixed literal (:106, never assembled at runtime); phase is @phase_teardown, a compile-time literal from a closed four-value vocabulary; schema=<schema_name> and tenant_id=<tenant_id> are the tenant under test and nothing else; schema_present_before_drop is a boolean-or-nil derived from the $1-filtered schemata read for THIS schema only; test_module and test_name come from ExUnit's own runner state via owning_test/0 and carry no tenant data. CLEAN: no other tenant's identifiers, no credentials, no connection string, no exception text -- log_teardown/3's rescue at :363 swallows silently rather than logging the exception. The wider capture report (format_report/1, :425-441) was checked too since it is the same new logging surface: all 14 fields are either this tenant's own values, values read through the $1-scoped queries above, static manifest data from tenant_scoped_migrations/0, or non-tenant scalars (db_now, pg_backend_pid); fields are selected explicitly rather than by dumping a struct, and registration_field/2 fetches only :provisioned_at and :migrations_applied_at. Registration itself carries no secret field (tenant_id/schema_name/migrations_applied_at). PER-INVARIANT VERDICTS. INV-1 Tenant data isolation: APPLIES / PASS -- applied per the role file's 2026-08-17 ISS-0026 correction (a diff touching tenant-scoped schemas is the common case, not the exception), even though no lib/ code changed. (a) scoping: every tenant-schema access is either schema-qualified to the derived name or tenant_id-predicated; the schema-qualified raw read is the raw-SQL equivalent of 0003's :prefix mechanism and is physically unable to reach another tenant's schema. (b) no migration in the diff -- nothing is created in public or anywhere else. (c) the tenant_id/schema relationship runs in the safe direction: the helper creates the tenant row, then DERIVES the schema name from that id via the pure schema_name_for_tenant/1, never accepting an independently-supplied tenant_id/schema_name pair that could disagree. INV-2 Server-side field authorisation: NOT-APPLICABLE -- no API response type, controller, plug or serialiser in the diff; S4 has not started. INV-3 Untrusted runtime sandboxing: NOT-APPLICABLE -- no Lua/WASM/script execution surface in the diff; S5 has not started. INV-4 Secrets by reference only: APPLIES / PASS -- the canonical grep run over the diff's added lines returns NO HITS; the only match for the secret-word heuristic anywhere in the new file is the string "tokens" at :139, a tenant table name in the completeness oracle, not a credential. No System.get_env, no connection string, no config change, and no secret is threaded into a log call, return value or handoff field. INV-5 Not-found/forbidden indistinguishability: NOT-APPLICABLE -- no lookup-by-ID endpoint; S4 has not started. INV-6 New data-access paths prove their scoping: APPLIES / PASS -- this handoff is the required proof artefact, status PASS, with per-invariant assessment recorded here. INV-7 No SQL string interpolation: APPLIES / PASS -- lib/ and priv/repo/migrations/ are unchanged, but the diff introduces raw SQL so the rule was applied to it directly: every value-bearing query is $1-bound, and the two identifier interpolations are provably confined to a regex-shaped derived schema name (see INV-F-9 above). No string-concatenated SQL carries tenant- or user-controlled data. INV-8 No unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths: NOT-APPLICABLE to shipped code (lib/letflow/ unchanged, no shared production process affected); checked against the new file anyway for completeness and it holds -- the five bare rows-map matches at :544/:554/:568/:580/:585 can each raise, but every one is reached only through guarded/2 (:520-524) or, for log_teardown/3, through guarded/2 plus the function's own rescue, with do_capture/2's outer rescue at :516 as the final net -- so no realistic failure escapes as an unhandled crash and, per INV-F-10, a failed observation degrades rather than turning a passing test red. TOOLCHAIN: MIX_ENV=test mix compile exits 0 (plain compile, no --warnings-as-errors, no mix format, per the ISS-0106 constraint). Zero warnings attributable to any of the three changed files; the type warnings emitted are pre-existing in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex, which this diff does not touch. OVERALL: PASS. No BLOCKER, MAJOR or MINOR security finding. One non-blocking OBSERVATION recorded below for the ISS-0112 39-site propagation.

issues.description: OBSERVATION, non-blocking, does NOT affect this PASS -- recorded because this helper is destined for 39 more call sites under ISS-0112, where a casual habit propagates. The teardown log line was the field-by-field subject of this gate and is clean, but the FAILURE paths log raw Exception.message(exception) into a Logger surface at test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:274 (assert_schema_complete!/2's capture_failed warning) and :382 (report_and_raise/3's capture_failed branch). That text is bounded in practice -- every query that can raise inside do_capture/2 is already scoped to the tenant under test, so a Postgrex.Error would name only this tenant's own schema/relation -- and it carries no credential, since Ecto/DBConnection do not put the password in an error message. It is therefore NOT an INV-4 violation and NOT an INV-F-8 leak today. The narrow residual is that a DBConnection.ConnectionError message can include host:port, i.e. connection endpoint detail rather than a secret, in a test-env log. Flagged only so ISS-0112 makes a deliberate choice about it before the pattern is copied 39 times, rather than inheriting it silently.

result.next_action: Proceed to WF-03 Step 3d (REVIEWER) -- the security gate is green and imposes no rework. SECURITY-REVIEWER requires no changes to test/support/tenant_fixture.ex or to either adopted test module. ORCH should carry the one MINOR OBSERVATION above into ISS-0112/GH#366 rather than into this run, since acting on it here would expand scope beyond the gate-approved design.
